question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party and Central Military Commission through ongoing elite reshuffles and military leadership purges that have removed potential rivals without disrupting his authority. As of mid-2026, he continues to set policy priorities, deliver major addresses on party history and modernization goals, and prepare for the 21st Party Congress in 2027, where analysts widely expect him to begin a fourth term with no designated successor in place. Trader consensus at 95.5% against removal by the end of 2026 reflects this entrenched position, the absence of visible factional challenges or institutional mechanisms for ouster, and historical patterns of prolonged rule by paramount leaders. Realistic scenarios that could still shift outcomes include a sudden health crisis or unforeseen elite realignment ahead of the congress.
